channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Trump says U.S. will impose 'economic D Day' against Iran
item.description: President Trump announced this week that the U.S. will be imposing the "most crushing economic operation" against Iran.

item.title: Iran has endured years of sanctions. Will Trump's economic pressure be effective?
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks to Miad Maleki, a former Treasury official who designed pressure campaigns for Iran, about the potential effectiveness of President Trump's pivot to "economic warfare."

item.title: Woman plotted to bomb the New York State Capitol building, authorities say
item.description: The FBI says it used a sting operation as part of an investigation into an alleged plot to bomb the New York State Capitol building in Albany.

item.title: As USS Lincoln heads home, mental health experts tally the stressors of life at sea
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln is now on its way home after spending nine months at sea. Experts weigh in on the mental health challenges of prolonged confinement and isolation aboard an aircraft carrier.

item.description: The American Repertory Theatre at Harvard University premiers a revival of Eugène Ionesco's landmark play, "Rhinoceros." NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer talks to director Diane Paulus and actor John Turturro.

item.title: Man on trial for death of rapper Tupac Shakur takes the stand
item.description: In Las Vegas, at the trial in the killing of Tupac Shakur, prosecutors provided what's expected to be the strongest evidence against Duane Davis, a former gang member implicated in the rapper's death.

item.title: 'It looked like a war zone': Spokane residents return home after devastating wildfire
item.description: Weeks after a wildfire destroyed hundreds of homes in Spokane, Washington, people are returning home. Big questions remain about whether it's really safe to return.
